narrate.explanation: Speak one short plain-text script with the fixed offline English (United States) eSpeak NG voice, or with one explicitly selected voice (en-gb, fr-fr or es), and publish a canonical PCM16 mono 22050 Hz WAV voiceover draft. The host captures the script bytes, refuses control characters, [[ ]] phoneme escapes, markup and text without words, runs the trusted espeak-ng with fixed arguments, and then re-synthesises the captured text in a separate process: every PCM byte must match. Choose it to create a first-pass narration to listen to, to time a script, or to feed a speech or archive step; it is synthetic, not a human recording, and a person must read the words and listen before publishing.
pitfalls: The speaking rate and an optional voice are the only authored synthesis choices. Without voice the fixed English (United States) voice speaks; with voice only en-us, en-gb, fr-fr or es are accepted. Pitch, amplitude, voice names or paths, variants, flags, SSML, phoneme codes, language detection and translation are rejected, not passed through.

The script must be plain words: control characters (including tabs, carriage returns and form feeds), [[ ]] phoneme escapes, SSML or other markup, and text with no letter or digit are refused with the offending code point; nothing is silently rewritten. The synthesizer may still expand numbers and abbreviations or ignore characters, so read the words as well as listening.

Verification needs the same trusted espeak-ng 1.52.0 with matching native data (--espeakng for run, or SCHEMAXIS_ESPEAKNG or a stored espeakng location for verify). A different build or voice data can change the samples and fail an older proof. Success proves consistent derivation only, not intelligibility, pronunciation, accent or accessibility.

A voice speaks the script as written by its own rules: Schemaxis does not detect or check the script language, translate it or correct it, so choose the voice that matches the language of the words (for example fr-fr for French text). The voice label is the one the runtime lists for that name, not a certificate of the accent or pronunciation you will hear.

examples.purpose: Narrate a literal two-sentence script at the default 175 words per minute.
Narrate a numbered, multi-line script from a UTF-8 text file at a slower 140 words per minute.
Narrate a literal script with the explicitly selected English (Great Britain) voice.
Narrate a French UTF-8 literal with the French (France) voice.
Narrate a Spanish UTF-8 literal with the Spanish (Spain) voice.
Narrate French, conform the narration with SoX and archive it as lossless FLAC.

narrate.question: When would you choose this operation, what does it produce, and what assumptions matter?

fields.explanation: Describe one narration: a script (text or source), an optional speaking rate and an optional voice. The script is captured as immutable bytes, spoken by the fixed eSpeak NG en-us voice or the one explicitly selected voice, and checked by a fresh native re-synthesis. The output is narration.wav (canonical PCM16 mono 22050 Hz) plus a JSON summary with the script and sound hashes.
pitfalls: Do not author voice names or paths, variants, flags, SSML, phoneme codes or markup: the only voice choice is the closed voice list. The result is a synthetic draft that a person must read and listen to.

/properties/version.explanation: Select the narration document contract. This identifies the authored structure, not the installed eSpeak NG release (1.52.0 is observed and checked at run time).
pitfalls: Use exactly schemaxis.espeakng/1; another value is refused before anything runs.

/properties/operation.explanation: Select the only operation, narrate: speak the script and publish narration.wav and espeakng-summary.json.
pitfalls: There is no other operation; a different name is rejected with UNKNOWN_FILTER.

/properties/text.explanation: The script to speak, written directly in the document: plain words, 1 to 1024 Unicode code points and at most 8 KiB of UTF-8. Use this for a short line or two; line feeds separate lines. It is captured exactly as written. Author exactly one of text and source.
/properties/text.units: Unicode code points (at most 1024) and UTF-8 bytes (at most 8192)
/properties/text.defaultMeaning: No default: exactly one of text and source is required.
pitfalls: Tabs, carriage returns, form feeds and other control characters, [[ ]] phoneme escapes, tags or character references such as <b> or &, and punctuation-only text are refused, never cleaned up. Use line feeds only.
Some symbols are read aloud by their native rules, numbers and abbreviations are expanded, and unsupported characters may be skipped; the sound can differ from what you expect, so listen and read.

/properties/source.explanation: Choose one absolute local UTF-8 .txt file holding the script, at most 1024 code points and 8 KiB, or bind a verified text or file artifact from an earlier step (for example a whisper.cpp transcript.txt). The file bytes are captured before synthesis and decide scheduler reuse. Author exactly one of text and source.
/properties/source.defaultMeaning: No default: exactly one of text and source is required.
pitfalls: The name must end in .txt; URLs, relative paths, symlinks and non-regular files are refused. The file must be valid UTF-8 without a byte-order mark and obey the same plain-text profile as text, with line feeds only.
Text exported by other tools often ends with a form feed or uses carriage returns; clean it with a tool you control, then choose the cleaned file.

/properties/rateWpm.explanation: Speaking rate in approximate words per minute, from 120 (slow and deliberate) to 240 (brisk). It scales how fast the fixed voice speaks; it does not change pitch or voice. Use the default for general narration, slow it down for instructions or clarity, speed it up for terse announcements.
/properties/rateWpm.defaultMeaning: Omitted means 175, the eSpeak NG default rate.
pitfalls: Only whole numbers from 120 to 240 are accepted (175.0, strings and booleans are refused). The actual duration depends on the words, numbers and punctuation, not only the rate, and a finished narration must stay within 120 seconds and 8 MiB.
Changing the rate changes the samples, so an earlier narration cannot be verified against a different rate.

/oneOf/0.explanation: Literal-script variant of the document: version, operation narrate, a text string, an optional rateWpm and an optional voice. The output is narration.wav plus espeakng-summary.json.

/properties/voice.explanation: Optionally choose which of four fixed offline eSpeak NG voices speaks the script: en-us (English, United States), en-gb (English, Great Britain), fr-fr (French, France) or es (Spanish, Spain). It selects the voice only: the script is not translated, language-checked or corrected, so pick the voice that matches the language of the words. Leave it out for the original English (United States) voice, whose plans and proofs are unchanged.
/properties/voice.defaultMeaning: Omitted means the original fixed en-us voice, exactly as before this option existed. An explicit en-us speaks the same synthesis but is recorded as an explicit choice.
pitfalls: Only the four listed names are accepted; other languages, regional or variant voices (such as en-gb-x-rp or fr-be), voice paths, MBROLA voices and automatic language detection are refused, not approximated.

Verification re-synthesises with the same voice in the trusted espeak-ng and needs that voice's native data; a runtime that does not list the exact voice is refused, because eSpeak NG would otherwise silently speak with a different voice. The label is what the runtime lists for the name, not a certificate of the accent heard, and no pronunciation, translation or original-speaker claim is made.
